title: Doctrine of eclipse (pre-Constitution laws and Part III)

content.statement: A pre-Constitution law inconsistent with a Fundamental Right is overshadowed and remains dormant to the extent of the inconsistency; it is not obliterated for all purposes and may revive if the inconsistency is later removed, subject to controlling judicial authority.
content.development: Developed in Indian constitutional adjudication on pre-Constitution laws under Article 13.
content.application: Use when analysing older statutes that pre-date the Constitution and Part III challenges.
exceptions: Post-Constitution laws inconsistent with Part III are void to the extent of inconsistency and are not merely eclipsed in the same sense
